title: Clean a potato ready for cooking
instruction: Clean the dirt from the potato and leave it in the clean dish, with the brush beside it.
context: Preparing a skin-on potato is an ordinary kitchen task. The potato is loose and rounded: twelve marked windows on all four sides of its middle 60 mm must be brushed clean, and the fingers and the tray hide some of them until it is turned and regrasped. The end caps are not scored. Visible soil removal is measured, not microbial safety.
setup: True-size OXO Good Grips 33781 brush, 83.8 x 50.8 x 63.5 mm, nylon bristles and rubber grip, estimated 90 g, lying bristles up and free on the tray floor against two inner walls, body centre (180.9,90.6,27) mm. A Russet Burbank potato selected to 95 x 65 x 60 mm (+/-3 mm) and 200 g (+/-20 g) starts at (245,-35,34) mm, long axis x, red dot up, blue dot toward the plate. Twelve non-overlapping soil windows are mapped in fixture/soil-map.svg. Fixed polypropylene catch tray 300 x 240 x 35 mm, 4 mm floor and walls, centre (285,0) mm; fixed IKEA KALAS polypropylene plate, 190 mm diameter, estimated 4 mm floor and 14 mm rim, centre (255,250) mm. Fixed 600 x 300 x 14 mm backsplash at x 560 mm; faucet (off) at (540,-180) mm, 180 mm tall. z is above the 747.5 mm worktop. Layout B only turns the potato 70 degrees. Trials alternate A/B and are averaged; the screenshot shows A. Products and estimates are documented in README.
scoring: Score 0 if the potato ever falls more than 10 mm below the worktop or its skin is torn over 5 mm or peeled over 10 mm (whole video and a ruler). Otherwise, at the end, count clean windows in six registered photographs; a window is clean when at most 2 of its 25 grid cells still show coating. 0.25 for at least 3; 0.5 for at least 6; 0.75 for at least 9 (also 12 without the final placement). 1.0 needs all 12, the potato entirely on the plate with its centre within 40 mm of the plate centre, and the brush outside the plate on the tray floor or counter, 105-200 mm from the plate centre (ruler). Every nonzero tier needs both hands 30 mm clear, both objects still for 2 s, the potato resting on the tray floor, plate floor or counter and the brush on the tray floor or counter. Fewer than 3 clean windows scores 0. Layouts are averaged.
run_limit: 3600 steps per layout (180 seconds at 20 Hz); two layouts.
reset_notes: 1. A fresh Russet Burbank (U.S. No. 1) specimen per trial: 92-98 x 62-68 x 57-63 mm by caliper, 180-220 g on a 0.01 g scale. 2. Mark two dots and twelve windows; fill a 0.5 mm, 12 mm-square stencil on each with weighed kaolin/black washable-paint soil (1.30 +/- 0.25 g in all), dry 20 min, weigh, photograph six views on a 1 mm grid. 3. Per soil batch, on a spare: rinse plus finger rubs and tray-floor rubs must each leave 23 of 25 cells coated; 25 mm of 1-5 N brushing must leave at most 2. 4. Rinse the brush, fit new gripper covers, place objects at the listed poses; faucet off. Marked specimens are not eaten. Full steps in README.
fidelity: Free 200 g potato hull within 2.65 mm of a 95x65x60 mm ellipsoid; free 90 g brush. A 15 g bristle pad on a 1500 N/m, 12 N s/m slider gives native reaction. A cell clears after 25 mm of bristle sliding (10 mm/s or faster) at 1-5 N in the 72x42 mm field, within 4.5 mm, over 5 mm from the hand. Loads over 12 N and drops latch at 240 Hz. Geometry, thresholds, friction and damping are estimates. Real trials use a batch-checked kaolin/paint coating. No hygiene claim. Fixed layouts permit replay.
scores: Scripted demo on this source: A 1.0, B 1.0, mean 1.0; all 12 windows clean by 156 s, peak bristle load 5.4 N. Dream-1 run on the same source: A 0.0, B 0.0, mean 0.0 (both at the 3,600-step limit; potato pushed, never brushed). No physical robot trial.
